posts.title: Things I Like: Elite Beat Agents (Nintendo DS)
posts.description: Elite Beat Agents was probably not one of the most famous Nintendo DS games, but I remember it quite well. It was one of the strangest titles to come out on the platform, especially if you didn’t know the context behind it. Nintendo had originally published a game in Japan called Osu! Tatakae! Ouendan, which was quite popular, so they decided to Americanize the concept and release a similar game in the United States called Elite Beat Agents. Unfortunately, it didn’t take off with the general public as well as Nintendo had hoped. It was definitely a strange concept, especially in American terms. Despite how much we love anime and video games, Ouendan is so deeply rooted in Japanese culture that translating it into an American product probably wasn’t the greatest idea from a marketing standpoint. posts.title: Fun Facts and Trivia About Black Friday
posts.description: Black Friday is the name given to the shopping day following Thanksgiving in the United States and is broadly understood as the unofficial opening of the Christmas shopping season for America. The phrase itself originated not in retail circles but on city streets. Philadelphia police officers in the 1950s and 1960s used it to describe the gridlock, packed sidewalks, and general disorder that descended on the city in the wake of Thanksgiving. A widely repeated explanation holds that the name refers to stores crossing from financial loss into profit, moving from “the red” into “the black.” Retailers later adopted this framing enthusiastically, but historians are in agreement that it was not where the term came from. Black Friday always lands on the Friday after Thanksgiving, which places it somewhere between November 23 and November 29 depending on the year. posts.title: Our Visit To The Carolina Rennaisance Festival (Charlotte, NC)
posts.description: Last year, when my wife was recovering from her surgeries, she couldn’t go to the Renaissance Faire around the same time. Her recovery was particularly difficult, so I promised her I’d take her to one in 2026, and I did. It was a little disappointing, though, because the people running our local event made so many mistakes. So I decided we should go to the big Renaissance Faire in Charlotte, North Carolina, which isn’t just a one-weekend event. Apparently it’s a two-month production, if not longer. And I have to say, it was definitely worth the trip. My wife got a black dress with a green cloak, and I bought her a green tiara. Or is it a diadem? I’m not quite sure, but it went perfectly with her outfit. I have to admit, I got really smitten with her during the Ren Faire. She looked so hot, and I just loved the dark-haired elven queen look.
